title: Semi-Analytical Pricing for General Default Intensity Models
authors: Ryan Parker, Mark Stedman, Luca Capriotti
abstract: Using the path-integral formalism, we develop an accurate and easy-to-compute semi-analytical approximation for a general class of {default intensity} models. We illustrate the accuracy of the method by presenting results for the Black-Karasinski model for which the proposed approximation provides remarkably accurate results, even in regimes of high volatility and multi-year time horizons. The accuracy and the computational efficiency of the proposed approximation makes it a viable alternative to fully numerical schemes for a variety of applications in econometrics and derivatives pricing, including the computation of XVA for credit products. As a practical example, we consider the pricing of a quanto Credit Default Swap (CDS) under stochastic intensity of default and an FX devaluation model.
summary: This paper introduces a semi-analytical approximation method based on the path-integral formalism for pricing derivatives under stochastic default intensity models. By generalizing the GTFK technique, the authors achieve high accuracy comparable to full numerical solutions while maintaining superior computational efficiency. This makes the method highly practical for applications like XVA calculation in credit risk management.
main_problem: The primary goal is developing an accurate, computationally efficient semi-analytical approximation for pricing derivatives under general default intensity models.
main_result: The proposed GTFK approximation provides remarkably accurate results for complex models like Black-Karasinski, offering a viable alternative to fully numerical PDE or Monte Carlo schemes.
method: The method utilizes the path-integral formalism, employing a specialized approximation (generalizing GTFK) that reduces the action integral by approximating it with a quadratic form around an optimized trial reduced density matrix.
model_or_system: The models are general default intensity processes where the intensity $h_t$ depends on a non-linear diffusion process $X_t$, exemplified by the Black-Karasinski and Hull-White models. These are applied to credit derivatives like Credit Default Swaps (CDS).
key_observables: Generalized Arrow-Debreu densities ($\psi_\lambda$), European option prices, and CDS spreads (in bps).
important_parameters: Volatility ($\sigma$), mean-reversion speed ($k$), time horizons ($T$), and market stress parameters.
main_assumptions: The approximation assumes the action can be accurately approximated by a quadratic form around an average path $\bar{x}$.
figures_summary: Table I compares credit spreads using GTFK vs. PDE/EE/KL for BK model; Table III shows spread comparison in Normal vs. Stressed markets; Table IV compares quanto CDS basis using GTFK vs. PDE.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem, develops the path-integral formalism and the GTFK approximation, validates its accuracy by comparing results against known numerical solutions (PDEs) for various models (BK), and applies it to practical pricing problems like quanto CDS.
why_interesting: While applied to finance, the core mathematical machinery—path integrals, reduced density matrices, and approximating complex dynamics with quadratic forms—shares conceptual parallels with techniques used in quantum field theory or open quantum systems modeling.
